rows.text: January 11, 2007
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
The Bank of Korea
Monetary Policy Decision
In the real economy, exports continue to show steady growth, facilities investment maintains a growing pace and construction investment appears to be recovering.
On the other hand, private consumption exhibits a slowdown in the pace of its expansion.
The Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
(The following is an English translation of the Monetary Policy Committee statement.)
Meanwhile, the current account has running a large surplus, thanks to the widened goods account surplus.
Consumer price inflation and core inflation both remain stable.
In the real economy, exports continue to show steady growth, facilities investment maintains a growing pace and construction investment appears to be recovering.
On the other hand, private consumption exhibits a slowdown in the pace of its expansion.
The upward pace of real estate prices has shown a signs of slowdown.
In the financial markets, overall liquidity conditions are favorable and financial institutions' lending has increased steadily.
Meanwhile, the current account has running a large surplus, thanks to the widened goods account surplus.

Taking the above economic and financial conditions into consideration, the Monetary Policy Committee of the Bank of Korea decided today to maintain the benchmark call rate (uncollateralized overnight rate) at its current level (4.50%) for the intermeeting period.
